section6.title: Frequently Asked Questions
section6.subtitle: Everything you need to know before buying in Tunisia.

faqs.q: Can a French citizen buy real estate in Tunisia?
faqs.r: Yes, absolutely. French and European nationals can freely purchase real estate in Tunisia, without nationality restrictions. Fund repatriation is guaranteed by the Central Bank of Tunisia (BCT). Only agricultural land requires prior authorization from the governor.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay taxes in France on Tunisian property?
faqs.r: The 1973 Franco-Tunisian tax treaty avoids double taxation. If you're a French tax resident receiving rental income in Tunisia, you declare this income in France and benefit from a tax credit for taxes already paid in Tunisia. We assist you with all these procedures.

faqs.q: What's the minimum budget to buy in Tunisia?
faqs.r: From €40,000 for an apartment in a secure residence in Hammamet or Sousse. For a villa with pool, count between €120,000 and €250,000 depending on location and size. These prices are 3 to 8 times lower than in France for equivalent quality.

faqs.q: Is it safe to buy in Tunisia in 2026?
faqs.r: Yes. Property rights are guaranteed by the Tunisian constitution and the land registry system (similar to French cadastre) legally secures your acquisition. CapTunisia systematically verifies property legality, absence of disputes, and accompanies you until signing at the notary.

faqs.q: How much does CapTunisia's support cost?
faqs.r: Our fees are transparent: €690 incl. VAT for the Essential pack, €990 incl. VAT for the Security pack (recommended), and €1,690 incl. VAT for the Premium pack with physical trip to Tunisia included. Check our /pricing page for all details.
